solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carelessly executed student operation controlled by secret agent

indicators.note: something controlled by another is held within its grip, so the first pair of pieces sits inside the agent

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
L is the learner plate, a student driver
OP is the short form of operation

explanation.surface: A student's clandestine operation, run by a spy, goes badly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Controlled by looks like it says who runs the operation, but it places both pieces inside the agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy work is slapdash and untidy, done without proper care or attention.

clue.text: Outrageous old priest lying about supporting case for secret weapon

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits underneath, so the reversed pair comes below the case letters
the case of a word is its outer shell, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of secret

indicators.note: lying about suggests turning around on the spot, so the pair of preceding words is read backwards

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, outrageous
Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A scandalous elderly cleric lies to cover up a hidden weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT+ELI reversed gives ILETTO, placed under ST in this down entry: STILETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger easily concealed about the person, hence a hidden arm.

clue.text: US writer, going short, taps working funds deliberately

indicators.note: to tap a barrel is to pierce into it, so the shortened writer goes into the money

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a purse is a sum of money, a fund or prize

indicators.note: going short means losing a bit, so the writer's name drops its final letter

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

explanation.surface: An American author who is running out of cash dips into the working capital on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps works as in tapping a cask: the shortened writer is let into the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on purpose means doing it intentionally, not by accident.

clue.text: Inferior wordplay oppresses king

indicators.note: to oppress is to weigh down from above, so in a down entry the wordplay piece sits on top of the king

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A poor joke weighs heavily on the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Punk is slang, chiefly American, for something worthless or of poor quality.

clue.text: Incendiary stuff from Heather? After a fashion

indicators.note: After places the heather piece behind the fashion piece in the answer

parts.note: a fashion or manner is a kind
ling is the common heather plant

explanation.surface: Something flammable comes from a woman called Heather, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling is small dry wood and twigs used to start a fire burning.

clue.text: Setter's job, ultimately, to deliver deceptive type?

parts.note: the setter is I, so setter's is I'm
a post is a job or position

indicators.note: ultimately points at the end, so only the final letters of the following words are kept

parts.note: the last letters of to and deliver

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's work, in the end, is to produce a trickster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits setters do in a sense deceive solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone else in order to cheat people, a fraud.

clue.text: Agency possibly elevating courses at Labour's expense?

definitions.text: Agency possibly elevating courses at Labour's expense?

parts.words: Agency possibly elevating courses at Labour's expense?
parts.note: surface reading: an organisation, perhaps a government body, boosting training courses funded by the Labour Party

parts.words: Agency possibly elevating courses at Labour's expense?
parts.note: setter's reading: a mechanical means of lifting meal courses between floors, doing away with the work of carrying them

explanation.surface: A government body promotes educational courses paid for by the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Courses are dishes of a meal, elevating is lifting, and the labour saved is the waiting staff's.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift carrying food from a kitchen to a dining room above.

clue.text: Exhausted editor (international) keeps still

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the abbreviation for international goes around the emptied word

parts.note: INT is the standard short form of international

indicators.note: an exhausted word has been emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of editor

explanation.surface: A worn-out newspaper editor, working internationally, stays motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: Exhausted reads as tired but here means emptied, leaving only the editor's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert lacks the power to move, so it is motionless or at rest.

clue.text: Entertaining girl, Georgia, bedding European roughly

indicators.note: bedding is putting to bed, so the state abbreviation tucks the next pieces inside it

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
E is the abbreviation for European
the suffix -ish means approximately

explanation.surface: A girl named Georgia rather crudely beds a European.
explanation.walkthrough: G(E ISH)A.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation to amuse guests.

clue.text: Measure included in maritime treaty

indicators.note: included in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of maritime and the start of treaty

explanation.surface: A provision written into an international agreement about the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The metre is the base unit of length, a standard measure of distance.

clue.text: Devilish fellow, Independent Nationalist, say, about to strike

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
I is the abbreviation for Independent
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation for say is written backwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: A mischievous independent nationalist politician is on the point of going on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To impinge on something is to hit or come into contact with it, have an impact.

clue.text: Ancient city grandeur Medici regularly displayed

parts.note: pomp is splendid display, grandeur

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the family name is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Medici

explanation.surface: An old Italian city shows off the Medici family's splendour time and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Desire without starting to acquire

indicators.note: without starting means losing the opening letter of the word for desire

parts.note: to yearn is to desire

explanation.surface: A longing to get something without first having to do the groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to gain or obtain it in return for work.

clue.text: How Observer and Spectator proceed with joint guide to the Times?

indicators.note: with puts the joint piece alongside the observing piece in the answer

parts.note: the wrist is the joint between hand and arm
observers and spectators go about things by watching

explanation.surface: How two weekly papers go about things alongside a guide to a rival daily.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer, The Spectator and The Times are British publications; here they are just lower-case watchers and times of day.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch tells you the hour, so it guides you to the times of day.

clue.text: Politician against alcohol… not a novel thing to write

definitions.text: not a novel thing to write

indicators.note: against means next to, leaning on, so the politician piece is placed right beside the drink piece

parts.note: shorts are spirits served in small measures, as opposed to long drinks such as beer
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A teetotal politician writes something hardly original.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Politician against alcohol' paints a temperance campaigner, but against only places one piece next to the other. Not a novel means too brief to be a full-length book.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief work of prose fiction is not long enough to count as a novel, though it is still written.

clue.text: Work hard in attempt to obtain prize

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the work and hard pieces sit within the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
OP is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Put in a lot of effort trying to win the cup.
explanation.walkthrough: TR(OP H)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other award given to a winner, an object won as a reward.

clue.text: Torrid Romeo's barred from local

indicators.note: barred means kept out, so the letter for Romeo is removed from the hot word

parts.note: torrid heat is tropical
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's is short for is

explanation.surface: A passionate Romeo has been banned from the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a pub in British English, and torrid here is a lover's passion, but both work as plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical can mean confined to one particular place or part, as with a topical ointment.

clue.text: Amanda and Sue lit up again and again

indicators.note: being lit up is being drunk, and drunken pieces stagger out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two women got drunk over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Lit up is slang for drunk; the two names together provide every letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad nauseam is Latin for to the point of sickness, used of something repeated tediously.

clue.text: What's previously affected that woman as well (briefly)?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the phrase for as well loses its last letter

parts.note: something hit by a change is affected by it
her is the pronoun for that woman
too means as well

explanation.surface: Asking what earlier on had an effect on a particular woman too.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitherto means until now, up to this point in time.

clue.text: Debris distributed randomly, not intentionally buried deep at first

indicators.note: randomly means in no set order, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not tells us those initial letters are taken away from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at first points at the opening letter of each of the three preceding words

parts.note: the initial letters of intentionally, buried and deep

explanation.surface: Rubbish scattered haphazardly, accidentally ending up buried far underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I, B and D from DISTRIBUTED and shuffle the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is loose waste material and fragments, rubbish left behind.

clue.text: I may have been pressed about vintage computer stuff

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a cru is a vineyard or grade of wine, a vintage
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A grape speaking: it may have been crushed over some vintage tech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressed' suggests grapes, prompted by vintage; here it is being press-ganged into the navy, as recruits once were.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruits to the navy were once forcibly enlisted by press gangs, so a recruit could say this.

clue.text: Consider hosting African group session to raise the spirits

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so the word for consider holds the group

parts.note: to see a point is to consider it
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: Think about hosting an African band for a cheering-up session.
explanation.walkthrough: SE(ANC)E. Raising the spirits sounds like lifting the mood; it is summoning ghosts.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a meeting where people try to contact the dead, calling up ghosts.

clue.text: Bring down the energy of meanest hound

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing the letter for energy lower rearranges the word by moving that one letter one place

parts.note: basest means most low and mean

explanation.surface: An instruction to deflate the vigour of a really nasty dog.
explanation.walkthrough: E is the physics symbol for energy; in BASEST it drops one place down the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged breed of hunting dog, a type of hound.

clue.text: Make a fuss: base disposed of old plane

indicators.note: disposed of means thrown away, so the base letter is taken out of the fuss word

parts.note: to create is to make a fuss in British slang
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A complaint that an air base has scrapped an ancient aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Base looks like an airfield beside the plane; it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Crate is slang for an old, ramshackle aeroplane or car.

clue.text: Vibes twice produced by some app involved with Mother Theresa

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so all the letters are mixed into a new order
twice tells us the jumbled letters make the answer two times over, so one copy is set aside

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Good feelings conjured up by a phone app linked to the famous nun.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual device: the twenty fodder letters are exactly enough for the answer two times over.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibes, short for vibrations, is the mood or feeling of a place, its prevailing air.

clue.text: Trump's expert general snatching victory

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing and holding, so the word for general takes the victory letter inside

parts.note: main means general, chief, as in the main body
V is for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: A US president's advisor, a military general who grabs a win.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump's flags an American word: mavin is US slang from Yiddish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mavin, or maven, is an American term for a connoisseur or specialist.

clue.text: Sound pleased, backing up bishop

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the two-letter word for up is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop sounds happy when his supporters rally round him.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat purrs when content, and people are said to purr when they show satisfaction.

clue.text: Hostile soldier leading unit

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the soldier piece comes before the unit piece

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: An unfriendly soldier in charge of a military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier means an army man in the surface; in crosswords it is often an ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as an adjective describes someone opposed or against something.

clue.text: One delivering various changes

indicators.note: changes means alters, so the letters of the adjective are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A courier bringing all sorts of alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: A saviour is someone who rescues others from danger, delivering them to safety.

clue.text: Fly back to hospital department function

indicators.note: back means returning the way it came, so the insect's name is read in reverse

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: Rush back to an outpatients' clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly looks like a verb meaning hurry; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the tangent is one of the standard functions of an angle, alongside sine and cosine.

clue.text: Numbers from East and West enthralling New York lyricist

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the numbers enclose the abbreviation for the city

parts.note: ten is a number, read from the west, normally
NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: the numbers are read in both directions: one copy from the west in normal order, the other from the east, right to left

parts.note: NOS is the abbreviation for numbers

explanation.surface: Figures from both sides of the world captivating a Manhattan songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Numbers serves twice: TEN read west to east, NOS read east to west as SON, and the two hold NY: TEN(NY)SON.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate, author of many lyric poems.

clue.text: Element of chemical analysis shed light on problem in recall

parts.note: to have lit something is to have shed light on it

indicators.note: recall means calling back, so the word for problem is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A chemistry concept clarifies a problem in memory.
explanation.walkthrough: Element suggests a chemical element; here it is just a component.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper is a basic chemistry tool showing whether a solution is acid or alkali.
